observation: Direct memory taps in independent 600-frame no-input and coin_start runs observe 5456 program-window halfword writes in each run, all from 68010 PC 0x02D35C, covering 0x800000-0x8048d6. The caller at 0x02C204 reads the same 32-bit source pointer 0x0001702E from $17000 and passes it to 0x02D2E0 in both runs. The pinned driver_68k_map maps that pointer into 68010 ROM, while the source-window probe observes no writes to 0x17000-0x25fff after frame 10. Normalizing the source-byte tap by the 68010 byte-lane masks yields 17 records totaling 2728 24-bit ADSP program words, including one explicit destination gap, followed by 0xff; this exactly accounts for the paired halfword writes. Source ownership is resolved as a ROM-resident upload stream; only the record semantics remain unresolved.
confidence: MAME-CONFIRMED ROM mapping plus OBSERVED-IN-TRACE pointer, writer PC, and transfer range
notes: The tap reports bus-level write events; paired halfword events arise from the 68010 MOVE.L transfer and are not yet normalized into instruction-level longwords.
The next experiment correlates the decoded 24-bit records with the ADSP snapshot and checks the ADSP data/control window.
